title.en: Past Ability (could / was able to / managed to)
title.es: La habilidad en el pasado (could / was able to / managed to)

text.en: English separates two cases for ability in the past. General ability: could (“When I was ten, I could swim.”), like the Spanish “podía” or “sabía”. Success on one specific occasion: was/were able to or managed to (“Yesterday, I was able to fix the car.”), like the Spanish “pude” or “logré”. Could does not work there. The negative, couldn’t, is correct in both cases.
text.es: El inglés separa dos casos para la habilidad en el pasado. Habilidad general: could («When I was ten, I could swim.»), como el «podía» o el «sabía» del español. Un logro en una ocasión concreta: was/were able to o managed to («Yesterday, I was able to fix the car.»), como el «pude» o el «logré» del español. Ahí could no funciona. La negación, couldn’t, sirve en los dos casos.

rows: imposible en el pasado (no pudo haber)

text.en: What someone was generally able to do during a period: could + base verb.
text.es: Lo que alguien podía hacer en general durante una época: could + verbo base.

examples.es: When I was ten, I could swim very fast.

tr.en: When I was ten, I could swim very fast.
tr.es: A los diez años yo podía nadar muy rápido.

examples.es: As a child, she could read before school.

tr.en: As a child, she could read before school.
tr.es: De niña ya podía leer antes de la escuela.

title.en: One specific success: was/were able to, managed to
title.es: Un logro concreto: was/were able to, managed to

text.en: When something worked out once, use was/were able to or managed to. Managed to also shows difficulty or effort.
text.es: Cuando algo se logró una vez, se usa was/were able to o managed to. Managed to además muestra dificultad o esfuerzo.

examples.es: The door was locked, but I managed to open it.

tr.en: The door was locked, but I managed to open it.
tr.es: La puerta estaba cerrada con llave, pero logré abrirla.

examples.es: Luckily, they were able to leave early.

tr.en: Luckily, they were able to leave early.
tr.es: Por suerte pudieron salir temprano.

text.en: After managed comes to + base verb, after succeeded comes in + verb-ing: “She succeeded in finding a job.”
text.es: Después de managed va to + verbo base, después de succeeded va in + verbo-ing: «She succeeded in finding a job.»

examples.es: She managed to pass the exam.

tr.en: She managed to pass the exam.
tr.es: Logró aprobar el examen.

examples.es: He succeeded in finding a job.

tr.en: He succeeded in finding a job.
tr.es: Consiguió encontrar trabajo.

title.es: Excepciones: couldn’t y los verbos de percepción

text.en: In the negative, couldn’t works for one occasion too: “I couldn’t open the door.” With see, hear, smell, understand, could is used even for one occasion.
text.es: En negativo, couldn’t sirve también para una ocasión: «I couldn’t open the door.» Con see, hear, smell, understand, could se usa incluso para una sola ocasión.

tr.en: I couldn't open the door.
tr.es: No pude abrir la puerta.

examples.es: At the top, we could see the whole city.

tr.en: At the top, we could see the whole city.
tr.es: Arriba pudimos ver toda la ciudad.

title.en: A missed chance: could have + participle
title.es: Una oportunidad perdida: could have + participio

text.en: You had the chance but it did not happen: “I could have won.” Couldn’t have + participle means it was impossible.
text.es: Tenías la oportunidad pero no ocurrió: «I could have won.» Couldn’t have + participio significa que era imposible.

examples.es: I could have won the game, but I made a mistake.

tr.en: I could have won the game, but I made a mistake.
tr.es: Podría haber ganado el juego, pero cometí un error.

examples.es: It couldn't have been Tom. He was away.

tr.en: It couldn't have been Tom. He was away.
tr.es: No pudo haber sido Tom. Estaba fuera.

text.en: Not “I didn’t could”: could is already past, and its negative is couldn’t. After could there is always the base verb: “I could swim”, not “I could swam”.
text.es: No «I didn’t could»: could ya es pasado, y su negación es couldn’t. Después de could siempre va el verbo base: «I could swim», no «I could swam».

text.en: A good reminder: the Spanish “podía” (ability) is usually could, and “pude” (specific success) is usually was able to or managed to. But “no pude” is couldn’t.
text.es: Un buen recordatorio: el «podía» (habilidad) suele ser could, y el «pude» (logro concreto) suele ser was able to o managed to. Pero «no pude» es couldn’t.

speak.en: English separates two cases for ability in the past. General ability: «could», for example «When I was ten, I could swim». Success on one specific occasion: «was able to» or «managed to», for example «Yesterday, I was able to fix the car». «Could» does not work there. The negative, «couldn't», is correct in both cases. Perception verbs like «see» and «hear» take «could» even for one occasion. A missed chance is expressed by «could have» plus the participle: «I could have won».
speak.es: El inglés separa dos casos para la habilidad en el pasado. Habilidad general: «could», por ejemplo «When I was ten, I could swim». Un logro en una ocasión concreta: «was able to» o «managed to», por ejemplo «Yesterday, I was able to fix the car». Ahí «could» no funciona. La negación, «couldn't», sirve en los dos casos. Los verbos de percepción, como «see» y «hear», llevan «could» incluso para una sola ocasión. Una oportunidad perdida se expresa con «could have» más participio: «I could have won».

items.sentence: When I was ten, I ___ swim very fast.

why.en: A general ability in the past: could.
why.es: Habilidad general en el pasado: could.

can.en: Can is present; the sentence is about the past (when I was ten).
can.es: Can es presente; la oración trata del pasado (when I was ten).

will be able to.en: Will be able to is future; the sentence is about the past.
will be able to.es: Will be able to es futuro; la oración trata del pasado.

examples: He could run very fast as a boy.

tr.en: When I was ten, I could swim very fast.
tr.es: Cuando tenía diez años, podía nadar muy rápido.

items.sentence: The door was locked, but I ___ open it with a knife.

why.en: Success on one specific occasion (I opened it): managed to.
why.es: Un logro en una ocasión concreta (la abrí): managed to.

could.en: Could marks a general ability; here it is one successful occasion. In casual speech you hear could, but for one concrete success the standard is was able to / managed to.
could.es: Could marca una habilidad general; aquí se trata de una sola ocasión lograda. En el habla informal se oye could, pero para un logro concreto el estándar pide was able to / managed to.

can.en: Can is present; the sentence is about the past (was locked).
can.es: Can es presente; la oración trata del pasado (was locked).

examples: He managed to fix the car.
We managed to catch the bus.

tr.en: The door was locked, but I managed to open it with a knife.
tr.es: La puerta estaba con llave, pero logré abrirla con un cuchillo.

items.sentence: Yesterday, the doctor ___ help us right away.

why.en: One specific occasion in the past (yesterday), and it worked: was able to.
why.es: Una ocasión concreta del pasado (yesterday), y salió bien: was able to.

could.en: Could marks a general ability; yesterday points to one specific occasion. In casual speech you hear could, but for one concrete success the standard is was able to / managed to.
could.es: Could marca una habilidad general; yesterday señala una ocasión concreta. En el habla informal se oye could, pero para un logro concreto el estándar pide was able to / managed to.

can.en: Can is present; yesterday points to the past.
can.es: Can es presente; yesterday señala el pasado.

examples: She was able to call him yesterday.
They were able to leave early.

tr.en: Yesterday, the doctor was able to help us right away.
tr.es: Ayer, el doctor nos pudo ayudar de inmediato.

items.sentence: She ___ finish the report last night. It was too long.

why.en: A negative in the past: couldn’t.
why.es: Un negativo en el pasado: couldn’t.

isn't able to.en: Isn’t able to is present; last night points to the past.
isn't able to.es: Isn’t able to es presente; last night señala el pasado.

can't.en: Can’t is present; the sentence is about the past (last night).
can't.es: Can’t es presente; la oración trata del pasado (last night).

tr.en: She couldn't finish the report last night. It was too long.
tr.es: Ella no pudo terminar el informe anoche. Era demasiado largo.

items.sentence: At the top of the hill, we ___ see the whole city.

why.en: A perception verb (see): could is used even for one moment.
why.es: Un verbo de percepción (see): could se usa incluso para un solo momento.

can.en: Can is present; the sentence is about the past.
can.es: Can es presente; la oración trata del pasado.

are able to.en: Are able to is present; the sentence is about the past.
are able to.es: Are able to es presente; la oración trata del pasado.

tr.en: At the top of the hill, we could see the whole city.
tr.es: En la cima de la colina, podíamos ver toda la ciudad.

items.sentence: After a long search, they succeeded ___ finding a cheap apartment.

why.es: Después de succeeded va in + verbo-ing.

to.en: After succeeded the word is not to but in + verb-ing (to goes with managed).
to.es: Después de succeeded no va to sino in + verbo-ing (to va con managed).

at.en: At does not follow succeeded; you need in + verb-ing.
at.es: At no va después de succeeded; hace falta in + verbo-ing.

examples: She succeeded in passing the exam.
He succeeded in finding a job.

tr.en: After a long search, they succeeded in finding a cheap apartment.
tr.es: Después de una larga búsqueda, lograron encontrar un departamento barato.

why.en: After managed comes to + base verb.
why.es: Después de managed va to + verbo base.

in.en: In goes with succeeded (succeeded in passing); managed takes to.
in.es: In va con succeeded (succeeded in passing); managed lleva to.

for.en: For does not follow managed; you need to + base verb.
for.es: For no va después de managed; hace falta to + verbo base.

tr.en: She managed to pass the exam.
tr.es: Ella logró pasar el examen.

items.sentence: He ___ able to open the window because it was stuck.

why.en: A negative in the past: wasn’t able to.
why.es: Un negativo en el pasado: wasn’t able to.

couldn't.en: Couldn’t does not take able to; couldn’t already expresses the ability by itself.
couldn't.es: Couldn’t no lleva able to; couldn’t ya expresa la habilidad por sí solo.

isn't.en: Isn’t is present; the sentence is about the past (was stuck).
isn't.es: Isn’t es presente; la oración trata del pasado (was stuck).

tr.en: He wasn't able to open the window because it was stuck.
tr.es: Él no pudo abrir la ventana porque estaba atorada.

items.sentence: I ___ won the game, but I made a mistake.

why.en: A missed chance: could have + participle (I could have won).
why.es: Una oportunidad perdida: could have + participio (podría haber ganado).

could.en: Could won is not possible; could would take a base verb, and a missed chance needs could have + participle.
could.es: Could won no es posible; could llevaría el verbo base, y una oportunidad perdida necesita could have + participio.

can.en: Can won is not possible; a missed chance needs could have.
can.es: Can won no es posible; una oportunidad perdida necesita could have.

examples: She could have gone with us.

tr.en: I could have won the game, but I made a mistake.
tr.es: Pude haber ganado el juego, pero cometí un error.

can't.en: Can’t is present; last night points to the past.
can't.es: Can’t es presente; last night señala el pasado.

items.sentence: In the end, the rain stopped and they ___ finish the game.

why.en: Success on one specific occasion (in the end they finished): were able to.
why.es: Un logro en una ocasión concreta (al final terminaron): were able to.

could.en: Could marks a general ability; here it is one successful occasion (in the end). In casual speech you hear could, but for one concrete success the standard is was able to / managed to.
could.es: Could marca una habilidad general; aquí es una sola ocasión lograda (in the end). En el habla informal se oye could, pero para un logro concreto el estándar pide was able to / managed to.

can.en: Can is present; the sentence is about the past.
can.es: Can es presente; la oración trata del pasado.

examples: We were able to leave early.

items.sentence: ___ you able to speak to her yesterday?

why.en: In a be able to question the be comes first: Were you able to…?
why.es: En una pregunta con be able to, be va primero: Were you able to…?

Did.en: After did comes the base verb; before able you need the verb be.
Did.es: Después de did va el verbo base; antes de able hace falta el verbo be.

Could.en: Could you able to is wrong; could already expresses ability and does not take able.
Could.es: Could you able to es incorrecto; could ya expresa habilidad y no lleva able.

tr.en: Were you able to speak to her yesterday?
tr.es: ¿Pudiste hablar con ella ayer?

items.sentence: He was so tired that he ___ keep his eyes open.

why.en: A negative in the past: couldn’t.
why.es: Un negativo en el pasado: couldn’t.

didn't could.en: Didn’t could is wrong: could is already past, and its negative is couldn’t.
didn't could.es: Didn’t could es incorrecto: could ya es pasado, y su negación es couldn’t.

can't.en: Can’t is present; the sentence is in the past (was so tired).
can't.es: Can’t es presente; la oración está en pasado (was so tired).

items.sentence: They managed ___ the last bus even though they were late.

why.en: After managed comes to + base verb: managed to catch.
why.es: Después de managed va to + verbo base: managed to catch.

catching.en: After managed there is no verb-ing (in + verb-ing goes with succeeded).
catching.es: Después de managed no va verbo-ing (in + verbo-ing va con succeeded).

catch.en: After managed the base verb needs to before it.
catch.es: Después de managed, el verbo base necesita to delante.

examples: We managed to leave on time.

tr.en: They managed to catch the last bus even though they were late.
tr.es: Lograron alcanzar el último autobús aunque se les hizo tarde.

items.sentence: Was she able ___ call you yesterday?

why.en: After be able comes to + base verb.
why.es: Después de be able va to + verbo base.

for.en: For does not follow able; you need to + base verb.
for.es: For no va después de able; hace falta to + verbo base.

in.en: In does not follow able; you need to + base verb.
in.es: In no va después de able; hace falta to + verbo base.

tr.en: Was she able to call you yesterday?
tr.es: ¿Ella te pudo llamar ayer?

items.sentence: We ___ have gone to the party, but we were tired.

why.en: A missed chance: could have + participle (we could have gone).
why.es: Una oportunidad perdida: could have + participio (podríamos haber ido).

can.en: Can have gone does not fit here; a missed chance is past: could have.
can.es: Can have gone no cabe aquí; una oportunidad perdida es del pasado: could have.

will.en: Will have gone is a future finished action; the sentence is about a past chance.
will.es: Will have gone es una acción terminada en el futuro; la oración trata de una oportunidad pasada.

tr.en: We could have gone to the party, but we were tired.
tr.es: Pudimos haber ido a la fiesta, pero estábamos cansados.
